s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic intermittent abdominal and lumbar pain with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Intermittent pain in right lumbar and abdomen
Herniation into the greater sciatic foramen
key_facts: CT examination shows proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis
CT examination shows herniation into the greater sciatic foramen

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic intermittent abdominal and lumbar pain with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Intermittent pain in right lumbar and abdomen
Herniation into the greater sciatic foramen
key_facts: CT examination shows proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis
CT examination shows herniation into the greater sciatic foramen

shortlist.label: Ureteral stone disease
shortlist.why_kept: Proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis on CT examination

shortlist.label: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
shortlist.why_kept: Proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis on CT examination

shortlist.label: Ureteral stricture
shortlist.why_kept: Proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis on CT examination

shortlist.label: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Herniation into the greater sciatic foramen with proximal ureteral dilatation

shortlist.label: Pyelonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic intermittent abdominal and lumbar pain with systemic symptoms and hydronephrosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of intermittent pain in the right lumbar and abdomen with chills and fever, which relieve with anti-inflammatory therapy but recur repeatedly, along with the CT findings of proximal ureter dilation and hydronephrosis, and herniation into the greater sciatic foramen, are most consistent with a ureteral stricture, which can cause obstructive symptoms and recurrent infections.

rejected.label: Ureteral stone disease
rejected.why: While possible, the lack of specific mention of stones on imaging and the nature of the symptoms suggest a more chronic obstructive process rather than intermittent obstruction from stones.

rejected.label: Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with more proximal obstruction symptoms and is less likely to cause the specific findings of herniation into the greater sciatic foramen.

rejected.label: Retroperitoneal fibrosis
rejected.why: This condition can cause ureteral obstruction but is less likely given the specific imaging findings and the lack of other systemic symptoms that often accompany retroperitoneal fibrosis.

rejected.label: Pyelonephritis
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms that could be consistent with pyelonephritis, such as fever and chills, the chronic nature of the symptoms and the specific imaging findings suggest a more structural issue like a ureteral stricture rather than an infectious process alone.
